# Why the woman in the white cap and green coat slows down after running

**Short answer: she was running to catch the bus that was pulling into the "Площадь Центральная" stop ahead of her. As soon as the bus finishes braking and comes to a complete standstill at the kerb, she can see that it is going to wait for her and that she will make it, so the reason for running disappears and she eases back down to a brisk walk while she covers the last few metres to the doors.**

## Who she is and where she is

The clip is a single panning shot of a snowy Russian city street (shopfronts reading ЧИТАЙ‑ГОРОД, СБЕРБАНК, BOTTICELLI LOUNGE CAFE, кафе‑пекарня), nominally following a road worker in an orange hi‑vis vest who is carrying an orange "40" speed‑limit sign along the roadway.

The woman in question enters at the right-hand edge of the frame in the very first seconds. A high-zoom crop of frame 1 shows her clearly: a white/cream knitted cap, a dark olive‑green padded coat with a tan fur ruff round the hood, black trousers and a grey handbag over her left forearm. She is on the far pavement, moving right to left, i.e. in the same direction as the traffic on that side of the road. Directly ahead of her on that pavement are the glass bus shelter with the stop name "площадь центральная" on it, a bright green kiosk, and — out in the nearside kerb lane of the far carriageway — a white-and-green LiAZ city bus, route 129, which is coming to a halt.

She is the only person in the whole 41-second clip who runs. Everybody else on that pavement is walking normally, and she goes past several of them at roughly twice their pace.

## The measurements that establish what happens

Because the camera is panning, image motion alone is misleading, so all positions below are measured relative to a fixed landmark in the scene (the green kiosk on the pavement), which removes the camera pan. Scale comes from the bus: a LiAZ‑5292 is 12 m long and spans about 990 pixels, so roughly 82 pixels per metre.

**The bus is still arriving and braking at the start of the clip, and stops at about t = 2.5 s.** Its position relative to the kiosk goes −462 px (t = 0), −712 (t = 1), −940 (t = 2), −986 (t = 3), −1020 (t = 4), −1016 (t = 5), −1022 (t = 6). That is a ground speed of about −250 px/s (≈3 m/s, ≈11 km/h) over the first two seconds, decaying to essentially zero from t ≈ 2.5 s onwards. In other words, in the opening seconds the bus is still rolling into the stop; shortly before the third second it comes to a complete standstill, and it then stands motionless at the kerb for the rest of the time it is visible (at least until t ≈ 9 s, by which time a second, articulated green bus has pulled in behind it).

**She is genuinely running at the start and has slowed to a walk by the end.** Her position relative to the same kiosk goes +111 px (t = 0), −112 (t = 1), −310 (t = 2), −508 (t = 3), −654 (t = 4), −776 (t = 5), −912 (t = 6), −980 (t = 6.5). Converting to speed over the ground:

| interval | speed |
|---|---|
| t = 0–1 s | ≈ 2.7 m/s (≈9.8 km/h) — a run/jog |
| t = 1–2 s | ≈ 2.4 m/s |
| t = 2–3 s | ≈ 2.4 m/s |
| t = 3–4 s | ≈ 1.8 m/s |
| t = 4–5 s | ≈ 1.5 m/s |
| t = 5–6.5 s | ≈ 1.7 m/s — an ordinary brisk walk |

So she loses roughly 40 % of her speed, and the drop is concentrated in the second half of the third second and the fourth second — that is, immediately after the bus has finished stopping.

**The gap between her and the bus tells the same story.** Measured from her to the rear corner of the bus: 7.0 m (t = 0), 7.3 m (t = 1), 7.7 m (t = 2), 5.8 m (t = 3), 4.7 m (t = 4), 2.9 m (t = 5), 1.3 m (t = 6), ≈1.0 m (t = 6.5). While the bus is still rolling she is running flat out and the gap is not closing at all — it is actually growing slightly, because the bus is moving faster than she can run. The instant the bus stops, the gap starts closing quickly even though she is slowing down. At about t = 6.7–7 s she reaches the back of the bus and passes out of sight behind it, heading for the doors, which are on the kerb side of the bus facing away from the camera.

## Why this explains the slow-down

Putting those three measurements together gives the causal chain:

* She starts the clip running because the bus she wants is arriving at the stop ahead of her and she is about seven metres short of it. That is the only thing in front of her, in the direction she is running, worth hurrying for.
* For the first two seconds the bus is still rolling forward faster than she can run, so running is the only way to have a chance; she cannot even close the gap.
* At about t = 2.5 s the bus comes to a full stop at the kerb by the "Площадь Центральная" shelter and simply sits there, taking on passengers.
* From that point on she is no longer chasing a moving target: she is walking to a stationary bus that is going to be there for several more seconds, and she is only a few metres away. The pressure is off, so she stops running and drops to a brisk walk, and then to something close to a normal walk, for the last stretch.
* She never stops, never turns, never breaks stride awkwardly — she just decelerates smoothly and continues straight to the bus, which is what "I no longer need to hurry" looks like, as opposed to any other cause.

## What does *not* explain it

It is worth stating explicitly what the footage rules out:

* **Not exhaustion.** She only runs for about three seconds, over perhaps seven metres, and she does not stop, bend over, or stagger; she settles into a steady, controlled walk and keeps that pace.
* **Not an obstacle, a slip or the ice.** The pavement she is on is cleared and she keeps a straight, even line; there is no stumble, no swerve, and nothing crosses her path. Other pedestrians walk the same stretch normally throughout.
* **Not because she gave up.** If she had decided she would miss the bus she would have stopped, or slowed to a genuinely slack pace, or turned back towards the shelter. Instead she keeps moving purposefully to the bus and goes behind it at its rear, where its doors are.
* **Not the camera or the road worker.** She never looks at the camera, and the road worker with the "40" sign is out in the carriageway on a different path; she neither reacts to him nor is impeded by him.

She slows down because the bus she was running to catch has finished pulling in and come to a complete stop at the bus stop just ahead of her — once it is standing still and she is only a few metres away, she is certain of catching it, so the urgency that made her run is gone and she covers the rest of the distance at a walk.
